song.title: Scene Seven_ I. The Dance of Eternity

genreClassification.rationale: Dream Theater is a foundational band in the progressive metal genre.

Ollama.targetTone: High gain, complex polyrhythmic lead tones with occasional clean arpeggiation.
gearHypotheses: Modern high-gain amp model (e.g., Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier or similar)

finalVerdict.targetTone: modern prog-metal high gain with tight rhythm attack

escalationReasons: draft is too generic for a signature part
possible wrong emphasis on lead vs rhythm texture
GP-180 could drift to generic modern metal

claudeFallback.targetTone: tight prog-metal rhythm with surgical note separation and clean contrast
corrections: prioritize rhythm tightness over lead drama
clean parts need separate preset path

finalVerdict.targetTone: tight prog-metal rhythm with surgical note separation and clean contrast
corrections: prioritize rhythm tightness over lead drama
clean parts need separate preset path

gp180.choicePolicy: Focus on modern, tight high-gain tones with extreme clarity and articulation.
gp180.bestMatchSummary: A highly articulate signal chain utilizing a boost/OD for attack definition, followed by a modern high-gain amp (Recti) paired with a 4x12 cabinet, complemented by chorus and delay for dynamic contrast.

blocks.purpose: Eliminate hum and background noise inherent in complex prog-metal recording.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for high-gain recordings.

blocks.purpose: Provide aggressive attack definition and tighten the palm-mute articulation (pick attack boost).
blocks.gap: None. Essential for achieving 'tight palm-mute attack'.

alternatives.reason: Could provide similar attack boost but might introduce unwanted coloration.

blocks.purpose: Provide modern, high-headroom gain structure without the 'fuzzy saturation blur' of older fuzz types.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated Mesa/Modern High Gain model. Distortion is chosen for its tight, articulate character.

alternatives.reason: Might be too aggressive or mid-scooped compared to the required modern tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the modern, high-gain character required for prog-metal while avoiding generic scoop.
blocks.gap: While Recti is a good choice, dedicated Mesa models are absent. This provides the necessary aggressive foundation.

alternatives.reason: Might sound too British or less modern than required.

blocks.purpose: Provide a tight, controlled low end and clear note separation under high gain.
blocks.gap: The ideal cabinet would be a modern 4x12 with scooped lows/tight mids. UK Vintage 4x12 is the best available option for tightness.

alternatives.reason: Might introduce too much low-end bloom, violating 'loose low-end rumble' avoidance.

blocks.purpose: Enhance note separation and clarity by surgically boosting mids and controlling excessive low-end rumble.
blocks.gap: None. Essential for 'clear note separation' in complex arrangements.

blocks.purpose: Provide the 'pristine clean arpeggios' and dynamic contrast needed for non-rhythm sections.
blocks.gap: None. Chorus is excellent for adding width to clean, sustained passages.

alternatives.reason: Too aggressive and distracting for the required 'pristine' sound.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle echo and space to lead lines without muddying the rhythm section ('light delay on leads').
blocks.gap: None. Standard tool for adding depth in progressive music.

alternatives.reason: Might sound too warm or vintage, detracting from the modern prog tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide subtle spatial depth for the overall mix without sounding overly wet or distracting.
blocks.gap: None. A gentle room reverb is ideal for maintaining clarity while adding dimension.

alternatives.reason: Can sound too artificial or metallic in a tight prog context.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment and master signal control.
blocks.gap: None. Standard final stage module.

warnings: The source material is highly technical prog-metal, requiring extreme clarity and articulation. The signal chain prioritizes modern high gain (Recti/Distortion) over classic rock tones to meet the 'tight' requirement.
Since dedicated Mesa/Modern High Gain models are unavailable, a combination of Distortion and Recti was used to simulate the desired aggressive, articulate tone.

improvements.summary: Upgrade cabinet realism for better note separation in high-gain rhythm parts.

proposals.reason: The current cabinet lacks the specific tight, modern character needed for prog-metal clarity.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased note separation and punchy low end.
